mn18:1.2: At one time the Buddha was living amongst the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Park.
mn18:2.1: Then, after dressing in the morning and taking his bowl and robe, the Blessed One entered Kapilavatthu for almsfood.
mn18:2.2: After collecting almsfood in Kapilavatthu and finishing his meal, he went to the Great Grove to pass the day.
mn18:2.3: He entered the Great Grove and sat at the root of a young Beluva tree.
mn18:3.1: Daṇḍapāṇi the Sakyan, while taking a walk for the sake of exercise, entered the Great Grove,
mn18:3.2: where he approached the Buddha and greeted him.
mn18:3.3: After finishing the appropriate polite greetings, he stood to one side leaning on a staff, and said to the Buddha,
mn18:3.4: “What does the contemplative say? What does he declare?”
mn18:4.1: “Venerable, I speak in such a way that no one in this world of angels, demons, gods, contemplatives, and priests, in this population of celestial and human beings, can argue with me; such that identifications do not persist in the subconscious of a holy person who is unbound by sensuality, who is free of doubt and inquietude, and who has no craving for either existence or non-existence.
mn18:4.2: “Venerable, this is what I say, this is what I declare.”
mn18:5.1: When this was said, Daṇḍapāṇi the Sakyan shook his head, stick out his tongue, and raised his eyebrows, wrinkling his forehead into three lines. Then he left, leaning on his staff.
